headline: Rare baby gorilla is born at the Detroit Zoo

sources.title: Detroit Zoo welcomes baby gorilla born on July 12; 2nd gorilla born in its history
Detroit Zoo welcomes newborn baby girl gorilla, the second born in nearly 100 years
Historic birth of baby gorilla girl at Detroit Zoo

chunks.text: The Detroit Zoo is celebrating a very special [[new arrival]]. Late in the evening on July 12, 2026, a baby girl gorilla was born to a [[first-time]] mother named Tulivu. This tiny [[infant]] is only the second gorilla to be born at the zoo in its nearly 100-year history. Staff members were [[thrilled]] when the healthy baby {{turned up}}, and they quickly {{gathered around}} to watch mother and baby together.

verbs.correct: To appear or arrive, often when not expected
verbs.wrong: To increase the level or amount of something

verbs.correct: To come together in a group near something

chunks.text: [[Keepers]] say that Tulivu {{took to}} motherhood [[right away]]. During her [[pregnancy]], she trained to {{sit through}} [[gentle]] [[ultrasound]] scans so the medical team could check on her baby. When the [[delivery]] finally came, she knew just what to do and never {{gave up}}. Right after the birth, she [[cradled]] her daughter and started to {{look after}} her [[with care]].

chunks.text: The new baby is a western lowland gorilla, a [[species]] that is critically [[endangered]] [[in the wild]]. Their numbers have {{fallen off}} [[sharply]] because of hunting and lost forests. Zoos [[across the country]] {{team up}} through a special [[breeding program]] to help the population grow. Each new birth adds to the genetic [[diversity]] that these animals need to [[survive]].

chunks.text: The zoo has not yet decided when visitors can {{drop by}} to meet the baby. Keepers do not want to [[rush]] into anything, and the timing will depend on what Tulivu needs as a new mother. For now, the family is {{settling in}} [[behind the scenes]] at the Great Apes of Harambee building. The baby is a [[half-sister]] to Motema, another young gorilla born at the zoo in 2024.

mainIdea.s: A rare baby gorilla turned up at the Detroit Zoo, only the second born there in nearly 100 years. The mother took to caring for her right away, and this helps an endangered species.
mainIdea.why: The story says the birth is only the second gorilla born at the zoo in almost 100 years, and it adds genetic diversity for this endangered species.

mainIdea.s: Keepers had to step in and feed the newborn gorilla themselves because the mother gave up on caring for her. The zoo now plans to let visitors drop by this week to see the baby.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the mother never gave up. She took to motherhood right away, and the zoo has not yet decided when visitors can drop by.

mainIdea.s: Two years ago, the same zoo opened a new water park exhibit for its sea lions and otters. Thousands of visitors lined up early on opening day just to watch the animals swim around.
mainIdea.why: This story is about a baby gorilla born at the Detroit Zoo in 2026, not an older water park exhibit for other animals.
